description: Patch releases of Redmine are automerged here, which is worth spelling out because the image's `/docker-entrypoint.sh` runs `rake db:migrate` on every single start unless `REDMINE_NO_DB_MIGRATE` is set, and this role does not set it. A bumped image therefore migrates the operator's issue tracker unattended and forward-only - the same shape of risk that keeps automerge off in other roles of this fleet.

It is safe for the patch class specifically, because Redmine's stable branches carry bugfixes and never new migrations. Measured rather than assumed: every consecutive pair of `X.Y.Z` tags in redmine/redmine from 4.0.0 through 7.0.0 was diffed over `db/migrate` - 67 patch spans - and exactly two of them touched that directory at all, both being a one-line edit to `20090503121505_populate_member_roles.rb`, a migration whose version is long since recorded in `schema_migrations` and which Rails therefore never re-runs. Not one patch release in four major lines added a migration file. Confirmed by experiment as well: installing 6.1.2's schema and then starting the 6.1.3 image against that same database applies zero migrations and goes straight to serving, while the same experiment across a minor (6.1.3 schema, 7.0.0 image) applies five - CreateWebhooks, AddIndexToUsersLowerLoginOnPostgresAndSqlite, AddIndexToUsersLogin, EnsureDefaultIssueStartDateToCreationDateIsStoredInDb and AddPrivateByDefaultToTrackers. The class that migrates is minor and major, and those remain human-reviewed pull requests.

The automerge branch is covered by three Molecule scenarios which do more than watch the unit turn active - which would prove nothing, since the unit carries `Restart=always` and an entirely unconfigured Redmine image serves a healthy 200 on `/` after falling back to SQLite. They assert that the container runs the image `redmine_version` resolves to and that the booted application reports that version; that the role's configuration.yml reached the process; that the env file did, including the `PORT` that decides which port Redmine binds; that the live ActiveRecord connection uses the adapter, socket, user and database the scenario configured; and that a project created inside the running Redmine is served back over HTTP and found in MariaDB, in Postgres or in the SQLite file, with no fallback store written alongside. A patch bump that broke startup, the schema, the configuration plumbing or the HTTP surface fails there before it can merge.

What no fresh-install test can see is an upgrade over an existing database, which is what the migration measurement above is there to cover. Should Redmine ever start shipping migrations in a patch release, the second extends line below is the one to drop.

`versioning=semver` on the annotation in defaults/main.yml is what keeps the noise out of that decision. docker.io/library/redmine publishes over 560 tags; strict semver leaves only the real `X.Y.Z` releases, because the flavour suffixes (`-alpine`, `-alpine3.24`, `-bookworm`, `-trixie`, `-passenger`) parse as prereleases and are skipped as unstable, while the floating `7`, `7.0`, `latest` and `alpine` tags are not versions at all. The flavour is carried separately in `redmine_distro` and composed into `redmine_container_image_tag`, so the annotation stays on the leaf literal Renovate can safely edit.
